answer: In an AI agent marketplace, each participant must lock stake proportional to claimed activity volume before opening an inlet for service requests. New identities cannot cheaply flood the terrace of available agents because the required collateral scales with expected throughput, forcing attackers to commit real capital per fake node. Honest agents recover stake after successful deliveries at the wharf of settlement, while sybils lose it on detected spam, raising the cost of attack far above potential gain.
